scenario.title: YELNYA OFFENSIVE - 2 SEP 1941
intro.text:
YELNYA OFFENSIVE - 2 SEP 1941

Yelnya, Southeast of Smolensk

You'll lead the attack against the semi-circular Yelnya salient which the Germans had extended 50 kilometres south-east of Smolensk, forming a staging area for an offensive towards Vyazma and eventually Moscow. Eliminate the threat and win the much-needed victory for us, Comrade!

ORDERS
a. Capture all VH!
b. Prevent that more than 9 enemy ground units reach the Exit Points.

CORE (recommended)
3x Tank (+1)
4x Infantry
1x Anti-Tank
2x Reconnaissance
1x Flak (+1)
3x Artillery
2x Fighter Aircraft
2x Tactical Bomber (+1)
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.reaction-briliant.text: The core escaped east of Minsk as an army, not a procession of fugitives. That distinction now amounts to most of the combat power in this camp.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.reaction-victory.text: Enough formations crossed the Minsk roads before they closed. Every headquarters stamp says withdrawal; every face in the column says defeat.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.reaction-tactical.text: Ten formations came out of the pocket. We counted them at dawn because in darkness the column looked too small to be an army.
line.reaction-lose.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.reaction-lose.text: The Minsk roads closed before the required formations escaped. What reached Yelnya is a headquarters, fragments of units, and an order to rebuild them while already fighting.
line.callback-choice-a.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.callback-choice-a.text: You ordered the core east before Minsk closed. Some call that why this command still exists. Others remember the units that reached our abandoned corridor ten minutes late.
line.callback-choice-b.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.callback-choice-b.text: You held the Minsk corridor for stragglers and recovered crews we are using now. We also escaped with enemy reconnaissance close enough to read the numbers on our last lorries.
line.scene-0.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.scene-0.text: Replacement tanks arrive with factory paint still tacky. Beside them stand crews who escaped Minsk without their machines. Neither group has trained together, but the attack timetable treats them as a division.
line.scene-1.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.scene-1.text: German traffic is already thinning behind the salient. They know the position is costly. If we strike slowly, we may capture the ground after they have removed the force that made it dangerous.
line.decision.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.decision.text: A concentrated blow may break the salient before the defenders withdraw. Rotating the assault echelons will preserve the rebuilt force, but gives the enemy more time to empty the pocket.
line.decision.choice.break-the-salient.t: Concentrate the rebuilt armour and artillery on one rupture, then fan out behind it.
line.decision.choice.break-the-salient.h: Attach an eight-strength BM-13 rocket-artillery detachment with 25 experience; priority issue and transport cost 100 prestige.
line.decision.choice.rotate-the-echelons: Attack in measured echelons and replace the leading formations before exhaustion stops them.
Restore the core to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition and give infantry 18 experience.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.choice-a-0.text: The survivors lead the route briefing; the new crews supply the machines. Once the line opens, mobile groups move for the exits instead of fighting every strongpoint.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-a-1.text: The new crews will believe the breakthrough proves they are veterans. Put the survivors at the head of every route conference and nowhere near the speeches afterward.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-b-0.text: No battalion stays forward simply because another has not arrived. Relief timings are orders, and the artillery programme moves with them.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.choice-b-1.text: Rotation keeps the formation neat and lets the salient empty by schedule. Give me one mobile group released the moment the first German road opens.
line.post-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.post-0.text: Put a Minsk survivor at every route table. The new crews have machines; let the men who lost theirs tell them where a road ends.
